subject: Economics
title: Macroeconomic objectives and the current account

stages.name: Macroeconomic objectives and the current account
stages.title: Macroeconomic objectives and the current account
stages.sub: Understand the four main macro objectives and why fixing the current account can conflict with the others.

steps.q: A government wants real GDP to rise year after year, giving people more goods and services. Which target is this?
steps.right: A target for the pace of economic growth
steps.wrong: A target for the rate of unemployment
steps.hint: Real GDP measures the size of output, not the number of people without jobs.

steps.q: A government wants as many people who are willing and able to work to actually have a job. Which target is this?
steps.right: A target for how many people are out of work
steps.wrong: A target for how fast prices are rising
steps.hint: This is about people without jobs, not about prices.

steps.q: A government wants prices to rise only slowly and predictably, not shoot up or crash. Which target is this?
steps.right: A target for the general price level
steps.wrong: A target for the size of output
steps.hint: This is about prices changing over time, not about how much is produced.
steps.pre: So another aim is a target for

steps.q: A government wants what the country earns from the rest of the world to roughly match what it spends abroad. Which target is this?
steps.right: A target for the country's trade with the rest of the world
steps.wrong: A target for the number of people in jobs
steps.hint: This is about money flowing in and out with other countries, not about jobs.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: Together, growth, jobs, prices and trade balance are the things every government tries to hit at once. What do we call this full set?
steps.right: The main goals a government tries to achieve for the economy
steps.wrong: The main taxes a government collects from households
steps.hint: Think of these four as one combined list of targets for the whole economy.

steps.q: A country running a large deficit decides to raise interest rates to attract foreign money and support its currency. Higher interest rates also make loans dearer for domestic firms and households. What is likely to happen to growth and jobs at home?
steps.right: They tend to slow down or fall
steps.wrong: They keep improving at the same pace
steps.hint: Higher interest rates make borrowing and spending harder for people and firms at home.
